name: halftone-reveal

frames.best_why: A clean circular patch of the sharp photograph sits over the dot print, so the reveal is unmistakable.

tagline: A dotted halftone portrait clears to a real photo under the cursor.
summary: A photograph printed as a coarse two-colour halftone. Where the pointer moves the dots swell open and the sharp picture shows through, and a click spreads a clearing ring across the print.
appearance: A smiling woman with dark hair and a red top fills the frame, rendered as large halftone dots in brick red against pale cream. Under the cursor a soft round patch turns smooth and photographic, showing her face and hair clearly.
behaviour: The whole picture stays as a dotted print while a soft-edged brush follows the pointer and converts the dots to the real photograph inside its reach. The revealed patch lingers briefly then fades back, and clicking sends a widening clear ring outward.
demo_content: A portrait of a smiling woman with dark hair and a red top against a warm outdoor background.
use_when: A hero or gallery image that should look printed until the visitor explores it with the pointer.
avoid_when: Reveal needs a mouse, so touch users only see the halftone, and the red ink fights other palettes.
customise: Set src plus fit, mode, dot shape, cell size, angle and the ink and paper colours. Reveal radius, softness, linger, reverse, wander and click burst are props.
weight_why: A full-screen halftone shader plus a brush mask pass run every frame while the pointer moves.

a11y.note: The photo is drawn to a canvas with no alt text or role, and the reveal answers only to a pointer.

issues: The top of the head is cropped off in every frame, so the portrait feels accidentally cut.
The dots are very large, so facial detail disappears outside the reveal.
polish_why: Convincing print texture and a satisfying reveal; the crop cuts the head and the dots are coarse.
title: Halftone Reveal
